findings_qualitative.value: C1-Sa drives a narrow, highly collimated, symmetric bipolar outflow extending ~12'' (0.3 pc)

evidence.quote: The outflow is highly-collimated and is seen to extend $\sim12\ensuremath{''}$ ($60,000\:$AU,$\:0.3\:$pc), and is quite symmetric

claims.hypothesis: C1-S hosts an early-stage massive protostar with ordered outflow
claims.experiment: ALMA 12CO(2-1), C18O, DCN and 1.3 mm continuum
claims.result: Collimated outflow from continuum peak C1-Sa near the C1-S center with matching velocity; momentum flux ~6e-3 Msun km/s/yr
claims.finding: C1-Sa is a good candidate early-stage massive protostar with ordered outflow/accretion

evidence.quote: We conclude that C1-Sa is a good candidate for an early-stage massive protostar

claims.hypothesis: C1-Sb is associated with the C1-S core
claims.experiment: C18O velocity and CO channel maps
claims.result: vLSR 81.36 km/s differs from the core's 79.4

evidence.quote: However, we cannot exclude the possibility that C1-Sb is also forming from the C1-S core.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Elongated CO filament interpreted as ambient gas rather than a collimated outflow, based on narrow velocity dispersion and lack of gradient

evidence.quote: The ambient nature of the filament is readily apparent in these figures.

limitations_admitted.value: Outflow properties are lower limits (Tex, inclination, optical depth); blue lobes affected by source overlap

evidence.quote: the absolute values of the above estimates should be viewed as lower limits

referee_caveats_inferred: Single inclination assumed (60 deg) with a large uncertain correction
Outflow length assumed 12'' for all lobes
Sidelobe contamination possible for fainter sources
